content.summary: The numerical contribution is framed accurately: the finite grid supplies one inequality, while a distinct assembled theorem proves the actual-support bound. Representation counts are explicitly separated from runtime claims. Both frozen snapshot and manuscript hashes match the inspected bytes. This review is confined to framing and source-interface checks; detailed grid reproduction is reserved for round five.

checks.method: Read manifest-verified SupportGrid53.lean and SupportFinish53.lean, and the F11/F12 compiler receipts.
checks.observation: The grid quantifies over bounded integer degrees; SupportFinish53 separately selects actual top degrees, supplies codegree and moment hypotheses, and invokes that leaf. Its conclusion concerns support(F), with no I(27) hypothesis. The receipts report exit zero for the support and equivalence roots. This supports the claimed distinction, subject to the stated retained-dependency trust.

checks.scope: Meaning and arithmetic of representation counts
checks.method: Computed 28n and binomial(n,4) with exact integers for n=85,72,56,53.
checks.observation: Results are 2380/2016/1568/1484 incidence bits and 2024785/1028790/367290/292825 subset variables, matching the manuscript. These count raw representations; they establish neither enumeration complexity nor measured speedup, as the text states.
